# ego-webqa

> Deterministic, MCP-native delivery QA for AI-generated web pages.

ego-webqa is a self-hosted Python MCP server and CLI. It renders a page with
Playwright, runs a narrow eight-viewport mobile matrix at 1x and 1.5x text
scale with and without safe-area insets, and returns reproducible evidence for
obvious layout, runtime, resource, and bounded CTA failures. Reports include
selector-level findings, repair directions, affected trigger combinations, and
commands that reproduce the run.

## Start

- Install the browser once: `ego-webqa install-browser`
- Install the MCP server: `uvx ego-webqa mcp`
- Run one CLI audit: `ego-webqa https://your-preview.example --out .qa/first-trial`
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/ego-webqa/
- Source: https://github.com/ROY32172310/qa
- Official MCP Registry: `io.github.ROY32172310/qa`
- 15-minute first-trial protocol:
  https://github.com/ROY32172310/qa/blob/master/docs/first-trial.md
- Result feedback:
  https://github.com/ROY32172310/qa/issues/new?template=result-feedback.yml

## MCP contract

The server exposes one tool, `audit_web_page`. It accepts a URL or a local
static directory and returns a pass/warn/fail decision with a compact Agent
summary and paths to the full JSON, JUnit, SARIF, screenshots, and governed
configuration evidence. Use it after generating or repairing a web page and
before claiming that page is ready to deliver.

## Boundaries

ego-webqa is a deterministic coarse gate, not a general QA platform. It does
not prove business-flow correctness, secure implementation, accessibility
compliance, visual-regression equivalence, cross-browser parity, or real-device
Safari compatibility. Playwright WebKit is not a real-device Safari claim.

The public site presents precomputed evidence. It does not accept arbitrary
URLs for server-side auditing.
